summary: Ryan examines the full scope of the gospel, arguing it's far broader than typical presentations. He critiques four common oversimplifications that emphasize different aspects—individual earthly blessing, individual eternal salvation, social justice, or church purity—while missing the comprehensive good news that God's kingdom has come to earth through Jesus. The gospel reconciles individuals to God, forms a new multi-ethnic family, and demonstrates kingdom values on earth now and for eternity.
key_points: The gospel in the first century was an announcement of a new king and kingdom, not just a spiritual message about the afterlife

Four common gospel oversimplifications: the 'coffee mug gospel' (earthly blessing), the 'evangelical gospel' (eternal fire insurance), the 'social gospel' (meeting physical needs or legislating morality), and the 'set apart gospel' (withdrawal from the world)
The cross is the center where all gospel implications meet—individual and corporate, earthly and eternal
The Lord's Prayer captures the full breadth of the gospel: individual provision, forgiveness, social transformation, and holy living
Salvation involves three steps: repent (change your mind), believe (change your allegiance), and be baptized (change your community)
big_idea: The gospel is the comprehensive good news that God's kingdom has come to earth through Jesus' life, death, and resurrection, inviting people to repent, believe, and be baptized into a new family that embodies kingdom values both now and for eternity.
title: FAQ: What is the Gospel?
